'''Bristow''': {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Mike Huckabee]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Mike Huckabee]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsAR}} The '''1998 Arkansas gubernatorial election''' took place on November 3, 1998 to elect the [[governor of Arkansas]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Mike Huckabee]] was re-elected to a second term in office over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee Bill Bristow. == Background == In 1993, Mike Huckabee won a [[1993 Arkansas lieutenant gubernatorial special election|special election]] to become [[Lieutenant Governor of Arkansas|lieutenant governor of Arkansas]] after [[Jim Guy Tucker]] was elevated to governor following the resignation of [[Bill Clinton]]. Tucker resigned from office in 1996 after his conviction for arranging fraudulent loans as part of the [[Whitewater controversy]], and Huckabee became governor of Arkansas on July 15, 1996.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/07/16/us/arkansas-governor-resigns-after-furor.html|title=Arkansas Governor Resigns After Furor|first=Steve|last=Barnes|newspaper=The New York Times|date=16 July (Democratic) * Keith Carle (Reform) * [[Mike Huckabee]], incumbent [[governor of Arkansas]] since 1996 (Republican) ===Campaign=== Because Huckabee had not yet been elected to the post, and the aftermath of Tucker's resignation had temporarily tarnished the title of governor, he was expected to face a strong challenge from Bristow. However, Huckabee's appeal as an honest [[Southern Baptist]] minister in the wake of scandal and Bristow's lack of political experience made Huckabee a much more attractive candidate.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/11/04/us/1998-elections-nation-governors-george-w-bush-re-elected-texas-his-brother-jeb.html|title=THE 1998 ELECTIONS: THE NATION -- GOVERNORS; George W. Bush Is Re-elected in Texas; His Brother Jeb Is Victorious in Florida|first=David E.|last=Rosenbaum|newspaper=The New York Times|date=4 November 1998}} He ran a well-funded grassroots campaign across all portions of the state, while the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] focused on [[Blanche Lincoln]]'s campaign for [[1998 United States Senate election in Arkansas|U.S. Senate]]. ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign=bottom !
